protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: after authJwtAud became configurable, local-RSA and HMAC jwt.Parse paths accepted correctly signed tokens without enforcing that audience; the remote verifier path enforced audience. GHSA-g962-2j28-3cg9 and published CVE-2026-30223 describe this exact authentication boundary failure.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CORRECTION_REQUIRED: 5fe07448584b9392f6763126fc72adf2151f66f1 is not the first-write because its parent dd11961a11ba27b6e65e4375f338b9fe1a981501 already has AuthJwtAud plus local/HMAC jwt.Parse calls without audience validation. The atomic public member is 5701bbc148dd3cb8d5ab62c630aecf2ac37314f8, which first introduces AuthJwtAud while leaving the already-existing local/HMAC parsers unwired.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: CONFIRMED for corrected BIC: parent 1d446ace04b18db19c6323bcb9e2de5a89a8c6e5 is present and verifiable; it has both local-RSA and HMAC jwt.Parse paths but no AuthJwtAud field or expected-audience control. Thus the advisory mechanism is absent in the immediate parent and first exists in 5701bbc148dd3cb8d5ab62c630aecf2ac37314f8.

findings: The vulnerability, direct fix, release boundary, and final NOT_AI classification are independently confirmed.

The primary record selects a later jwt/v5 refactor member as BIC even though that member's immediate parent already exhibits the advisory condition; introducing a remote-path WithAudience contrast did not originate the local/HMAC audience bypass.

PR #264 member 5701bbc148dd3cb8d5ab62c630aecf2ac37314f8 is the smallest reconstructable first-write: it introduces the expected audience configuration while retaining local/HMAC parsing without enforcement, and its immediate parent lacks the expected-audience configuration entirely.
Because the corrected BIC is also human-authored and has no AI marker, the verdict remains NOT_AI despite the causal-field correction.

corrected_fields.flaw_origin: The flaw begins when PR #264 member 5701bbc148dd3cb8d5ab62c630aecf2ac37314f8 introduces AuthJwtAud and audience-aware remote OIDC verification but leaves the pre-existing local-RSA and HMAC jwt.Parse paths without any audience enforcement. Parent 1d446ace04b18db19c6323bcb9e2de5a89a8c6e5 contains those parsers but no AuthJwtAud, so it cannot exhibit the configured-audience bypass. Squash f13a5c070a4397865b287f598058a25f68d42ad3 lands the same patch on main. Later PR #269 member 5fe07448584b9392f6763126fc72adf2151f66f1 changes the remote implementation to jwt/v5 WithAudience but merely preserves the already-existing local/HMAC omission.
